speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the nature of your cough, such as whether it is productive or dry, and how long has it been occurring? Do you have a history of smoking or significant environmental exposures?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience shortness of breath or wheezing, and have you ever been diagnosed with cystic fibrosis or primary ciliary dyskinesia? I would also like to know if you have any history of nasal polyps or chronic sinusitis. REQUEST TEST: High-Resolution CT Chest

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the copious purulent sputum and recurrent bronchitis with a normal HRCT, I need to rule out structural airway abnormalities. Do you experience hemoptysis, weight loss, or night sweats, and have you ever had an episode of severe pneumonia or aspiration in the past? REQUEST TEST: Bronchoscopy with Bronchoalveolar Lavage

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the CT and bronchoscopy are normal, I need to evaluate for functional airway disorders. Do you experience wheezing, chest tightness, or shortness of breath that varies in intensity or responds to bronchodilators? REQUEST TEST: Spirometry with Bronchodilator Response

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: FVC: Reduced, FEV1: Reduced, FEV1/FVC Ratio: Normal

speaker: Doctor
text: The spirometry suggests a restrictive pattern rather than obstructive disease, so I need to evaluate for parenchymal lung involvement. Do you experience progressive shortness of breath on exertion, and have you noticed any clubbing of your fingers or toes? REQUEST TEST: Pulmonary Function Tests with Diffusing Capacity (DLCO)

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: FVC: Reduced, FEV1: Reduced, FEV1/FVC Ratio: Normal

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal HRCT and bronchoscopy make structural diseases like bronchiectasis unlikely, yet the chronic productive cough persists. Given the restrictive pattern on PFTs, I need to evaluate for interstitial lung disease or neuromuscular issues. Do you experience joint pain, skin rashes, or difficulty swallowing, and have you noticed any muscle weakness? REQUEST TEST: Serum Autoimmune Panel

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal imaging, bronchoscopy, and autoimmune panels, I must consider functional causes like laryngopharyngeal reflux or chronic rhinosinusitis with post-nasal drip. Do you experience heartburn, regurgitation, or a sensation of fluid in your throat, and do you have a constant need to clear your throat? REQUEST TEST: 24-hour pH Impedance Monitoring

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the copious purulent sputum and recurrent infections with normal imaging and autoimmune workup, I must consider a diagnosis of exclusion like Diffuse Panbronchiolitis or Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia. Do you have a history of hearing loss, infertility, or chronic sinusitis, and have you noticed any nasal polyps? REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Aggressive cough with thick, yellow-green sputum. I also have Cough worse in the morning, History of recurrent bronchitis.

speaker: Doctor
text: You have two questions remaining. Do you have a family history of similar respiratory issues, and have you experienced any nasal congestion or chronic sinusitis? REQUEST TEST: Sweat Chloride Test

speaker: Doctor
text: With cystic fibrosis and primary ciliary dyskinesia ruled out, the chronic productive cough, morning worsening, and recurrent infections in a non-smoker with normal imaging strongly suggest Diffuse Panbronchiolitis, particularly if there is an Asian ancestry. DIAGNOSIS READY: Diffuse Panbronchiolitis
